title: Don't Get Played
paragraphs: What's up, Galatia! It's Paul, and my whole crew here in the faith is sending greetings to the Galatian churches. Just so we're clear, my authority for writing this doesn't come from some popularity contest or from getting appointed by some important human higher-up. It comes directly from Jesus the Messiah and God the Father, who raised him from the dead. I'm God-commissioned. So I'm greeting you with the great words — grace and peace! We know what those words mean, because Jesus Christ rescued us from this messed-up world by offering himself as a sacrifice for our sins. God's plan is that we all experience that rescue. Glory to God forever! Oh, yes!
§ The Real Message

I'm actually stunned right now. I can't believe how quickly you guys turned traitor on the One who called you by the grace of Christ, embracing a totally different message. And this isn't some minor remix, you know — it's completely other, an alien message, a no-message, a lie about God. The people stirring up all this agitation among you are turning the Message of Christ on its head, twisting it around. Let me be blunt: If one of us — even if an angel dropped down from heaven! — preached something different from what we preached originally, let him be cursed. I said it once, I'll say it again: If anyone, regardless of reputation or credentials, preaches something different from what you received originally, let him be cursed.

Do you think I'm saying all this to manipulate crowds? Or to get on God's good side? Or to win popular applause? If my goal was popularity, I wouldn't bother being Christ's slave. Know this — I'm dead serious here, friends — this great Message I delivered to you is not mere human optimism. I didn't receive it through the traditions, and I wasn't taught it in some school. I got it straight from God — I received the Message directly from Jesus Christ.

You've probably heard the story of my earlier life, back when I lived the Jewish way. In those days I went all out in persecuting God's church — I was systematically destroying it. I was so fired up about my ancestors' traditions that I shot head and shoulders above my peers in my career. But even back then, God had his eye on me. When I was still in my mother's womb, he chose me and called me out of sheer generosity! Then he stepped in and revealed his Son to me, so that I might joyfully tell the non-Jews about him.

Right after that, I didn't waste time consulting anyone around me. I didn't even go up to Jerusalem to confer with the guys who were apostles long before me. I just got away to Arabia for a while, then came back to Damascus. It was a full three years before I finally went up to Jerusalem to compare stories with Peter. I was only there fifteen days — but what days they were! Except for our Master's brother James, I saw no other apostles. I'm telling you the absolute truth in this.

After that, I started my ministry in the regions of Syria and Cilicia. Even after all that time, the Christian churches in Judea didn't know my face. The only report they ever heard was: "That man who once persecuted us is now preaching the very message he used to try to destroy!" Their response was to recognize and worship *God* — because of *me*!

title: Paul Puts Peter on Blast
paragraphs: § What's Central?

Fourteen years after that first visit, Barnabas and I went up to Jerusalem, and we took Titus along with us. I went to lay out before them what had been revealed to me — I placed before them exactly what I was preaching to the non-Jews. I did this in private with the leaders, the ones held in esteem by the church, so our concern wouldn't turn into some controversial public issue, marred by ethnic tensions — I wasn't about to let years of work get exposed to denigration and my present ministry put at risk. And here's the significant part: Titus, non-Jewish though he was, was NOT required to get circumcised. While we were in conference, we were infiltrated by spies pretending to be Christians, who slipped in to find out just how free true Christians really are. Their ulterior motive was to reduce us to their brand of servitude. We didn't give them the time of day. We were determined to preserve the truth of the Message for you.

As for those considered important in the church — their reputation doesn't impress me. God isn't impressed with mere appearances, and neither am I. And of course these leaders were able to add nothing to the message I'd been preaching. It soon became clear that God had entrusted me with the same message to the non-Jews that Peter had been preaching to the Jews. When James, Peter, and John — the pillars of the church — recognized that my calling had come from God, they shook hands with me and Barnabas, assigning us to ministry among the non-Jews while they kept reaching out to the Jews. The only additional thing they asked was that we remember the poor — and I was already eager to do that.

Later, when Peter came to Antioch, I confronted him face-to-face, because he was clearly out of line. Here's the situation: earlier, before certain persons had come from James, Peter regularly ate with the non-Jews. But when that conservative group came from Jerusalem, he cautiously pulled back and put as much distance as he could manage between himself and his non-Jewish friends. That's how fearful he was of the conservative Jewish clique pushing the old system of circumcision. Unfortunately, the rest of the Jews in the Antioch church joined in that hypocrisy — so that even Barnabas was swept along in the charade.

But when I saw that they weren't keeping a steady, straight course according to the Message, I spoke up to Peter in front of them all: "If you, a Jew, live like a non-Jew when you're not being observed by the watchdogs from Jerusalem, what right do you have to require non-Jews to conform to Jewish customs just to make a favorable impression on your old Jerusalem buddies?"

We Jews know that we have no advantage of birth over "non-Jewish sinners." We know very well that we are not set right with God by rule-keeping but only through personal faith in Jesus Christ. How do we know? We tried it — and we had the best system of rules the world has ever seen! Convinced that no human being can please God by self-improvement, we believed in Jesus as the Messiah, so that we might be set right before God by trusting in the Messiah — not by trying to be good.

Have some of you noticed that we are not yet perfect? (No great surprise, right?) And are you ready to make the accusation that since people like me — who go through Christ to get right with God — aren't perfectly virtuous, Christ must therefore be an accessory to sin? That accusation is ridiculous. If I went back to "trying to be good," I'd be rebuilding the same old barn that I tore down. I'd be acting as a pretender.

Here's what actually took place: I tried keeping rules and working my head off to please God, and it didn't work. So I quit being a "law man" so that I could be God's man. Christ's life showed me how, and enabled me to do it. I identified myself completely with him. Indeed, I have been crucified with Christ. My ego is no longer central. It's no longer important that I appear righteous before you or have your good opinion, and I'm no longer driven to impress God. Christ lives in me. The life you see me living is not "mine" — it's lived by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. I'm not going back on that.

Is it not clear to you that going back to that old rule-keeping, peer-pleasing religion would be an abandonment of everything personal and free in my relationship with God? I refuse to do that — to repudiate God's grace. If a living relationship with God could come by rule-keeping, then Christ died unnecessarily.

title: Seriously, Who Played You?
paragraphs: § Trust Christ, Not the Rules

You crazy Galatians! Did someone put a spell on you? Have you taken leave of your senses? Something crazy has happened — it's obvious you no longer have the crucified Jesus in clear focus in your lives. His sacrifice on the cross was certainly set before you clearly enough.

Let me put this question to you: How did your new life begin? Was it by working your heads off to please God? Or was it by responding to God's Message to you? Are you going to continue this craziness? Only crazy people would think they could complete by their own efforts what was begun by God. If you weren't smart enough or strong enough to begin it, how do you suppose you could perfect it? Did you go through this whole painful learning process for nothing? It's not a total loss yet, but it certainly will be if you keep this up!

Answer this question: Does the God who lavishly provides you with his own presence — his Holy Spirit — working things in your lives you could never do for yourselves, do these things because of your strenuous moral striving, or because you trust him to do them in you? Don't these things happen among you just as they happened with Abraham? He believed God, and that act of belief was turned into a life that was right with God.

Isn't it obvious? People who put their trust in Christ — not people who put their trust in the law! — are like Abraham: children of faith. It was all laid out beforehand in Scripture: God would set things right with non-Jews by *faith*. Scripture anticipated this in the promise to Abraham: "All nations will be blessed in you."

So those who live by faith are blessed along with Abraham, who lived by faith — this is no new doctrine! And that means anyone who tries to live by his own effort, independent of God, is doomed to failure. Scripture backs this up: "Utterly cursed is every person who fails to carry out every detail written in the Book of the law."

The obvious impossibility of carrying out such a moral program should make it plain: no one can sustain a relationship with God that way. The person who lives in right relationship with God does it by embracing what God arranges for him. Doing things for God is the opposite of entering into what God does for you. Habakkuk had it right: "The person who believes God, is set right by God — and that's the real life." Rule-keeping doesn't naturally evolve into living by faith; it only perpetuates itself in more and more rule-keeping. Scripture noticed it too: "The one who does these things [rule-keeping] continues to live by them."

Christ redeemed us from that self-defeating, cursed life by absorbing it completely into himself. Remember the Scripture that says, "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree"? That's what happened when Jesus was nailed to the cross: he became a curse, and at the same time dissolved the curse. And now the air is cleared — we can see that Abraham's blessing is present and available for non-Jews, too. We are *all* able to receive God's life, his Spirit, in and with us by believing — just the way Abraham received it.

Friends, let me give you an example from everyday affairs, about the free life I'm talking about. Once a person's will has been signed, no one else can annul it or add to it. Now, the promises were made to Abraham and to his descendant. Notice how Scripture, in the careful language of a legal document, doesn't say "to descendants" — everybody in general — but "to your descendant" (the noun, note, is singular), referring to Christ. Here's how I read it: a will, earlier signed by God, is not annulled by an addendum attached 430 years later, wiping out the promise of the will. No — this addendum, with its instructions and regulations, has nothing to do with the promised inheritance in the will.

So what's the point of the law, the attached addendum? It was a thoughtful addition to the original covenant promises made to Abraham. The law's purpose was to keep a sinful people in the way of salvation until Christ (the descendant) came, inheriting the promises and distributing them to us. Obviously this law was not a firsthand encounter with God — it was arranged by angelic messengers through a middleman, Moses. But if there's a middleman, like at Sinai, then the people aren't dealing directly with God, are they? The original promise, though, is the *direct* blessing of God, received by faith.

If that's the case, is the law an anti-promise — a negation of God's will for us? Not at all. Its purpose was to make it obvious to everyone that we are, in ourselves, out of right relationship with God — and so to show us the futility of devising some religious system to get by our own efforts what we can only get by waiting in faith for God to complete his promise. If any kind of rule-keeping had the power to create life in us, we would certainly have gotten it by now.

Until we were mature enough to respond freely in faith to the living God, we were carefully surrounded and protected by the Mosaic law. The law was like those Greek tutors you're familiar with, who escort children to school and protect them from danger or distraction, making sure the children really get to the place they set out for.

But now you've arrived at your destination: by faith in Christ, you're in direct relationship with God. Your baptism in Christ wasn't just washing you up for a fresh start — it also dressed you in an adult faith wardrobe: Christ's life, the fulfillment of God's original promise.
§ In God's Family

In Christ's family there can be no division into Jew and non-Jew, slave and free, male and female. Among us you are all equal — we are all in a common relationship with Jesus Christ. And since you're Christ's family, you're Abraham's famous "descendant" — heirs according to the covenant promises.

title: From Kid to Heir
paragraphs: Let me show you what this means. As long as the heir is a minor, he's no better off than a slave. Legally he owns the entire inheritance, but he's under tutors and administrators until whatever date his father set for emancipation. That's how it was with us: when we were minors, we were like slaves, ordered around by simple instructions — the tutors and administrators of this world — with no say in how our own lives were run.

But when the time set by God the Father arrived, God sent his Son — born among us of a woman, born under the conditions of the law — so he could redeem those of us kidnapped by the law. Now we've been set free to experience our rightful heritage. You can tell for sure you're fully adopted as his own children, because God sent the Spirit of his Son into our lives, crying out, "Papa! Father!" Doesn't that privilege of intimate conversation with God make it plain you're not a slave, but a child? And if you're a child, you're also an heir — with complete access to the inheritance.

Earlier, before you knew God personally, you were enslaved to so-called gods that had nothing divine about them. But now that you know the real God — or rather, since God knows you — how can you possibly go back and subject yourselves to those tin gods? Because that's exactly what you're doing when you get intimidated into scrupulously observing all the traditions, taboos, and superstitions tied to special days and seasons and years. I'm afraid all my hard work among you is going up in a puff of smoke!

My dear friends, what I'd really love is for you to try to put yourselves in my shoes — the same way I, when I was with you, put myself in yours. You were so sensitive and kind back then. You never came down on me personally. You knew very well that the reason I ended up preaching to you was that I was physically broken — I couldn't continue my journey, so I was forced to stop with you. That's how I came to preach to you.

And don't you remember? Even though taking in a sick guest was the most troublesome thing, you treated me as well as you'd have treated an angel of God — as well as you'd have treated Jesus himself if he'd shown up. What happened to the satisfaction you felt back then? Some of you would have given me your very eyes if you could have — that's how deeply you cared! And now have I suddenly become your enemy just by telling you the truth? I can't believe it.

Those heretical teachers go to great lengths to flatter you, but their motives are rotten. They want to shut you out of the free world of God's grace so you'll always depend on them for approval and direction — which makes them feel important.

Being passionate about doing good is a great thing — just not only when I'm around. Can't you keep the same concern for me and my message while I'm away that you had when I was with you? Do you know how I feel right now — and how I'll feel until Christ's life becomes visible in your lives? Like a mother in the pain of childbirth. Oh, how I wish I were with you! Then I wouldn't be reduced to this blunt, letter-writing language out of sheer frustration.

Tell me, you who are so in love with the law: have you actually paid close attention to that law? Remember Abraham — he had *two* sons: one by the slave woman, one by the free woman. The son of the slave woman was born by human plotting; the son of the free woman was born by God's promise. This is a perfect picture of what we're dealing with now. The two births represent two ways of being in relationship with God. One is from Mount Sinai in Arabia — it matches what's going on in Jerusalem right now: a slave life, producing slaves as offspring. That's the way of Hagar. But there's an invisible Jerusalem, a free Jerusalem — and she is our mother. That's the way of Sarah. Remember what Isaiah wrote: "Rejoice, barren woman who bears no children, shout and cry out, woman who has no birth pangs, because the children of the barren woman now surpass the children of the chosen woman." Isn't it clear, friends, that you — like Isaac — are children of promise? Back in the days of Hagar and Sarah, the child who came from faithless plotting (Ishmael) harassed the child who came, empowered by the Spirit, from the faithful promise (Isaac). Isn't it clear that the harassment you're getting now from the Jerusalem heretics follows that old pattern? Scripture tells us exactly what to do: "Expel the slave mother with her son, for the slave son will not inherit with the free son." Isn't that conclusive? We are not children of the slave woman — we are children of the free woman.

title: Don't Get Chained Up Again
paragraphs: § The Free Life
Christ has set us free to live a free life. So take your stand! Never again let anyone put a harness of slavery on you.

I'm emphatic about this: the moment any of you submits to circumcision — or any other rule-keeping system — at that same moment, Christ's hard-won gift of freedom is squandered. I repeat my warning: the person who accepts the ways of circumcision trades all the advantages of the free life in Christ for the obligations of the slave life of the law.

I don't think you'd ever intend this, but here's what happens: when you try to live by your own religious plans and projects, you're cut off from Christ — you fall out of grace. Meanwhile, we're expectantly waiting for a satisfying relationship with the Spirit. In Christ, neither our most careful religion nor throwing religion out the window amounts to anything. What matters is something far more interior: faith expressed in love.

You were running superbly! Who cut in on you, deflecting you from the true course of obedience? This detour doesn't come from the One who called you into the race in the first place. And please don't toss this off as insignificant — it only takes a minute amount of yeast, you know, to permeate an entire loaf of bread. Deep down, the Master has given me confidence that you will not defect. But the one who is upsetting you — whoever he is — will bear the divine judgment.

As for the rumor that I still preach circumcision (like I did in my pre-Damascus Road days) — that's absurd. Why would I still be persecuted, then? If I were preaching that old message, no one would be offended if I mentioned the Cross now and then — it would be so watered-down it wouldn't matter one way or the other. Why don't these agitators, obsessive as they are about circumcision, go all the way and cut themselves off completely!

It's absolutely clear: God has called you to a free life. Just make sure you don't use this freedom as an excuse to do whatever you want and wreck your freedom. Instead, use your freedom to serve one another in love — that's how freedom grows. Everything we know about God's Word boils down to a single sentence: Love others as you love yourself. That's an act of true freedom. But if you bite and ravage each other, watch out — in no time at all you'll be annihilating each other, and where will your precious freedom be then?

My counsel is this: live freely, animated and motivated by God's Spirit. Then you won't feed the compulsions of selfishness. There's a root of sinful self-interest in us that's at odds with a free spirit, just as the free spirit is incompatible with selfishness. These two ways of life are opposites — you can't live one way sometimes and the other way other times, depending on how you feel that day. Why not choose to be led by the Spirit, and escape the erratic compulsions of a law-dominated existence?

It's obvious what kind of life grows out of always trying to get your own way: repetitive, loveless, cheap sex; a stinking pile of mental and emotional garbage; frenzied, joyless grabs for happiness; trinket gods; magic-show religion; paranoid loneliness; cutthroat competition; all-consuming-yet-never-satisfied wants; a brutal temper; an inability to love or be loved; divided homes and divided lives; small-minded, lopsided pursuits; the vicious habit of turning everyone into a rival; uncontrolled, uncontrollable addictions; ugly parodies of community. I could go on. This isn't the first time I've warned you, you know — if you use your freedom this way, you will not inherit God's kingdom.

But what happens when we live God's way? He brings gifts into our lives, the way fruit appears in an orchard — things like affection for others, exuberance about life, serenity. We develop a willingness to stick with things, a sense of compassion in the heart, and a conviction that a basic holiness permeates things and people. We find ourselves in loyal commitments, not needing to force our way in life, able to marshal and direct our energies wisely.

Legalism is helpless when it comes to producing this — it only gets in the way. Among those who belong to Christ, everything connected with getting our own way and mindlessly going along with what everyone else calls "necessities" has been killed off for good — crucified.

Since this is the life we've chosen — the life of the Spirit — let's make sure we don't just keep it as an idea in our heads or a warm feeling in our hearts, but work out its implications in every detail of our lives. That means no comparing ourselves with each other, as if one of us were better and another worse. We have far more interesting things to do with our lives. Each of us is an original.

title: Squad Up and Stay Real
paragraphs: § Nothing but the Cross

Live creatively, friends. If someone falls into sin, forgivingly restore him — and save your critical comments for yourself. You might be needing forgiveness before the day is out! Stoop down and reach out to those who are oppressed. Share their burdens, and so complete Christ's law. If you think you're too good for that, you're badly deceived.

Take a careful look at who you are and the work you've been given, and then sink yourself into that. Don't be impressed with yourself. Don't compare yourself with others. Each of you has to take responsibility for doing the creative best you can with your own life.
And be very sure about this: you who've been trained to a self-sufficient maturity — enter into a generous common life with those who trained you, sharing all the good things you have and experience.

Don't be misled: no one makes a fool of God. What a person plants, that's what he'll harvest. The person who plants selfishness — ignoring the needs of others, ignoring God! — harvests a crop of weeds. All he'll have to show for his life is weeds! But the one who plants in response to God, letting God's Spirit do the growth work in him, harvests a crop of real life — eternal life.

So let's not get fatigued doing good. At the right time we'll harvest a good crop if we don't give up or quit. Right now, then, every time we get the chance, let's work for the benefit of all — starting with the people closest to us in the community of faith.

Now, in these last sentences, I want to emphasize — in the bold scrawls of my own handwriting — how immensely important what I've written to you is. These people trying to force circumcision on you have only one motive: they want an easy way to look good before others. They lack the courage to live by a faith that shares Christ's suffering and death. All their talk about the law is gas — they don't even keep the law themselves! And they're super picky about which laws they do keep. They only want you circumcised so they can boast about recruiting you to their side. That is contemptible!

As for me, I'm going to boast about nothing but the Cross of our Master, Jesus Christ. Because of that Cross, I've been crucified in relation to the world — set free from the stifling atmosphere of pleasing others and fitting into the little patterns they dictate. Can't you see the central issue here? It's not about what you and I do — submit to circumcision, reject circumcision. It's about what *God* is doing — and he's creating something totally new, a free life! All who walk by this standard are the true Israel of God — his chosen people. Peace and mercy on them!
Quite frankly, I don't want to be bothered by these disputes anymore. I have far more important things to do — the serious living of this faith. I bear in my body scars from my service to Jesus.
